identity.title: FuXi-Ocean: A Global Ocean Forecasting System with Sub-Daily Resolution

problem.claim: Enable accurate, high-resolution global ocean forecasting for maritime operations and environmental monitoring.

gap.claim: Traditional numerical models are computationally intensive at fine scales, while data-driven methods generally operate daily and struggle with sub-daily error accumulation.

contributions.claim: Introduces FuXi-Ocean, a data-driven global ocean forecasting model targeting six-hourly, eddy-resolving 1/12° predictions to depths of 1500 meters.
Combines context-aware feature extraction and stacked-attention prediction with a Mixture-of-Time module that learns variable-specific reliability across temporal contexts.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe FuXi-Ocean as the first data-driven global ocean model achieving the stated six-hourly, 1/12° eddy-resolving resolution and 1500-meter depth.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report comprehensive experiments showing superior skill for temperature, salinity, and currents across multiple depths.

narrative_sequence.summary: High-resolution ocean forecasts are important, but conventional numerical models are costly and fine-scale accuracy is difficult to maintain.
Recent data-driven approaches improve computational efficiency but typically remain daily and accumulate errors in sub-daily forecasting.
FuXi-Ocean targets six-hourly global forecasts at 1/12° resolution and uses temporal-context integration through the MoT module.
The authors report superior prediction skill for key ocean variables across depths.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a specific failure mode—error accumulation in sequential sub-daily prediction—to a targeted mechanism that combines multiple temporal contexts and learns variable-specific reliability.

lessons.interpretation: A strong abstract can make the method–problem relationship explicit by matching a named mechanism to a named limitation.
lessons.application: When presenting a forecasting method, state the operational failure mode first, then identify which component is intended to address it and how.
lessons.exception: Avoid this framing when the proposed component is not directly motivated by a clearly stated failure mode or when the abstract lacks supporting evaluation.

unknowns: The abstract does not report quantitative metrics, baselines, dataset details, forecast lead times, or the conditions behind the claimed superior skill.
The stated first-of-kind distinction is author-reported and is not independently verified here.
